description: Return who writes the fund letters in the index. Without cik: the SEC registrants (usually fund trusts) whose N-CSR and N-CSRS reports hold indexed letters, newest letter first, each with letter, fund and named-company counts; q searches the registrant, manager or fund name. With cik: one writer's profile, its ten newest letters with links and the companies its letters name most, with stance counts. It is an index with links: no letter text is returned. Stances and counts are FinancialMD's reading of the letters (by rule or by a named model), not the manager's statement and not advice. Use it to find a fund family's letters or what companies a writer discusses; then call fund_letters with cik for the letters themselves.

as_of.description: Knowledge date or timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339). The answer is what FinancialMD knew at that instant: only facts whose known interval contains as_of. Omit for the current view.

cik.description: Registrant CIK for one writer's profile; omit to list writers.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page (data.next_cursor).

limit.description: Maximum number of periods or items to return (default 10, at most 100).

q.description: List only: part of the registrant, manager or fund name.

name: fund_letter_investors

outputSchema.description: The FinancialMD envelope (docs/API.md section 2): data plus meta (request_id, as_of knowledge time, matched company, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base). Every numeric value inside data is an object with value, unit, currency, period, known interval, restated flag, method and a proof pointing at the filing. On failure the result is isError with an error object instead.

data.description: List: { items: [{ id, registrant_cik, name, manager, manager_slug, filer_cik, letters, funds, companies_named, first_published, latest_published, links }], next_cursor, note }. With cik: the same fields for one writer plus recent_letters: [{ id, kind, title, fund, period_end, published, source_url }] and companies: [{ company, letters, investors, stances }].

error.description: Present only on isError results: the API error code and message plus remedy hints.

meta.description: Request metadata: request_id, as_of, company resolution, coverage, pipeline_version, licence, terms, proof_base.

attribution.description: Citations a source requires on anything shown from the answer.
